correctness.rationale: For all admissible continuously strictly decreasing wind-speed elasticities, differentiating the risk/power ratio gives E-3 below rated wind speed and E above. This exactly classifies either one maximum or two maxima separated by a rated-speed minimum. Endpoint asymptotics, positive wind-density level integration and an exchange inequality prove unique feasibility and global optimality at every nontrivial cap. The ratio cutoff 3/10 in the explicit R=v^4 exp(-v), rated=2 model meets exact exponential inequalities. CHECK.py reproduces antiderivatives, all four boundaries, and a strict energy gap; finite grids are explicitly only supplementary.

originality.rationale: The classical integral-budget exchange principle and prior environmental-curtailment approaches are not original and are expressly acknowledged. Actual claim-level searches and examination of Whitby 2024, Peterson 2021, Maclaurin 2022, Rogers 2020, and RENEBAT II public summary did not yield the complete sharp iff risk-elasticity criterion for two wind-speed curtailment bands, its budget window, and the strict one-cutoff loss. Priority remains provisional because the full RENEBAT II report was inaccessible.
residual_risks: The full 2016 RENEBAT II report could not be read; its summary describes risk-yield curtailment optimization, and a stronger theorem in that report cannot be ruled out.
General optimal-control frameworks may contain equivalent implications not recognized in accessible inspected sections; a subsequent independent literature audit is needed.
Historical priority is provisional; absence of an indexed exact-match result is not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The explicit necessary-and-sufficient local risk-elasticity condition identifies when a widespread single cut-in-speed policy class must be suboptimal under a mathematically natural fixed wildlife-risk cap. It supplies a nontrivial analytic boundary and a certified constructive counterexample. Mathematical value is a structural decision-rule limitation, not empirical proof that real turbine risk profiles exhibit two bands.
